title: 2nd Stopping Place 5th Truth Universal And Particular Order And Wisdom Indicating An All Powerful All Wise One

questions.question: What main quality does the passage say can be seen in everything, from the whole universe down to small parts of the human body?
questions.answer: A careful and wise order can be seen in all of them.

questions.question: What are two big examples of order mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The overall plan of the universe and the earth’s daily and yearly movements.

questions.question: What are two small human examples of order mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: A person’s face and the movement of blood cells.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone can truly act on things in a deliberate and creative way?
questions.answer: Only the One who has complete power and complete wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage describe all other things besides that One?
questions.answer: They receive what is done to them, show His works, and do not act on their own.

questions.question: What three things are needed for putting things in order for a purpose?
questions.answer: Knowledge, wisdom, and willful choice.

questions.question: What does the passage say the many useful arrangements in the world prove about the Creator?
questions.answer: They prove that the Creator is one and acts with will and choice.

questions.question: According to the passage, through what does everything begin to exist?
questions.answer: Through His power.

questions.question: According to the passage, through what does a thing take a certain condition?
questions.answer: Through His will.

questions.question: According to the passage, through what does a thing receive its particular form?
questions.answer: Through His choice.

questions.question: The world is compared to a hospice. What does that comparison help show?
questions.answer: It helps show that the world is like a place prepared for living guests and cared for by one generous Master.

questions.question: What are some examples of “oneness” given in the world?
questions.answer: The lamp is one, the time-marker is one, the sponge is one, the cook is one, the drink is one, and the field is one.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude from these many examples of oneness?
questions.answer: The Maker and Owner of the world must also be one.

questions.question: What character trait of the Maker is shown by serving living guests through many great servants?
questions.answer: His great generosity and hospitality.

questions.question: Name three Divine Names listed in the passage.
questions.answer: All-Wise, Compassionate, and Quickener.

questions.question: What does the passage say about these Names, attributes, and actions in the world?
questions.answer: They are one, they reach everywhere, and each is present in every place.

questions.question: How do the Divine Names and actions relate to one another?
questions.answer: They support and complete one another so closely that they seem joined together.

questions.question: In the example about giving life, what happens when the Name of Quickener appears?
questions.answer: Other Names like Creator, Giver of Form, and Provider also appear at the same time in the same system.

questions.question: What final belief does this harmony of Names and actions prove?
questions.answer: It proves that the One shown by these Names and the Doer of these actions is one, single, and unique.

questions.question: What idea is repeated through the passage from the largest things to the smallest?
questions.answer: Everything shows a planned order.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both the universe and blood cells?
questions.answer: To show that the same order appears in both huge things and tiny things.

questions.question: What does the passage say no one besides the Absolutely Powerful and Absolutely Wise can do?
questions.answer: No one else can purposely and creatively control any thing.

questions.question: What does “passive” mean in the passage when speaking about created things?
questions.answer: It means they do not independently direct themselves but receive what is done to them.

questions.question: Why can order for useful goals only come from knowledge and wisdom?
questions.answer: Because reaching goals in the best way requires understanding and wise planning.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect regularity with will and choice?
questions.answer: Because choosing one form and one arrangement out of many possibilities needs willing and choosing.

questions.question: What does the passage say the ordering of the universe clearly proves about its Creator?
questions.answer: It proves the Creator is one and acts by will and choice.

questions.question: Match each idea with the right word from the passage: bringing into being, giving a state, giving a form.
questions.answer: Bringing into being is by power, giving a state is by will, and giving a form is by choice.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use for the world to make the idea easier to understand?
questions.answer: It describes the world as a hospice.

questions.question: What do the many examples of “one” in the world lead the reader to understand?
questions.answer: They lead the reader to understand that the Master of the world is one.

questions.question: Besides being one, what two qualities of the Master are highlighted?
questions.answer: Great generosity and care for guests.

questions.question: Who are the “guests” in this hospice picture?
questions.answer: The living creatures in the world.

questions.question: What kinds of things are listed together near the end: Names, attributes, or actions?
questions.answer: All three are listed together.

questions.question: Name one attribute and one action mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: Mercy is an attribute, and nurturing is an action.

questions.question: What does it mean that each Name and act is present everywhere?
questions.answer: It means their effects can be seen throughout the world, not in only one place.

questions.question: How does the example of the Name of Quickener support the message of unity?
questions.answer: It shows that many Divine works appear together at the same time in the same pattern, pointing to one Doer.

questions.question: How does the passage end its message?
questions.answer: It ends by saying that the believers accept and affirm this truth.

questions.question: What does the first paragraph teach about the universe and the human body?
questions.answer: Both show a detailed order set by wisdom.

questions.question: What does the phrase about “universal or particular” help explain?
questions.answer: It explains that the order covers everything, both large and small.

questions.question: Give one example from nature and one example from a person that show this order.
questions.answer: The earth’s regular turning is one example, and the blood’s cell movement is another.

questions.question: What does the passage say about any created thing trying to control another thing by itself?
questions.answer: It says no created thing can purposely and creatively do that on its own.

questions.question: How are created things described instead?
questions.answer: They are described as receivers and displays of what is done by Allah.

questions.question: What must exist before something can be arranged for a useful result?
questions.answer: Knowledge, wisdom, will, and choice must exist.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the order brings many benefits before our eyes?
questions.answer: It means the usefulness of the order is clear and can be noticed directly.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from this beneficial order?
questions.answer: The One who creates and manages all beings is one and acts intentionally.

questions.question: What is the difference between power, will, and choice in the passage?
questions.answer: Power brings things into existence, will gives them a certain condition, and choice gives them a distinct form.

questions.question: Why does the passage list many “one” examples in the world?
questions.answer: To strengthen the proof that the world has one Maker.

questions.question: What does the image of a hospice suggest about how the world is run?
questions.answer: It suggests the world is prepared and managed with care for those living in it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Maker’s treatment of living beings?
questions.answer: He serves them generously through many great servants.

questions.question: What can we learn from the Names being active in every corner of the world?
questions.answer: We can learn that Allah’s rule and care reach everywhere.

questions.question: Why is it important that the same Names and actions are found in all places?
questions.answer: Because this shows one Lord is at work everywhere, not many separate powers.

questions.question: How do the Names and actions “complement” one another?
questions.answer: They fit together perfectly and support each other in one united pattern.

questions.question: Which other Names appear together with the Name of Quickener in the example?
questions.answer: Creator, Giver of Form, and Provider.

questions.question: What does the same instant and same system show in that example?
questions.answer: It shows unity, coordination, and one Doer behind all of them.

questions.question: What truth is said to be certain and obvious from all this?
questions.answer: That the One shown by these Names and actions is one, single, and unique.

questions.question: What feature of creation is the passage focusing on most?
questions.answer: It is focusing on the wise order found everywhere.

questions.question: How wide is the range of this order according to the passage?
questions.answer: It stretches from the whole universe to tiny parts inside a human body.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the face, senses, and blood cells?
questions.answer: To show that careful order appears even in very close and detailed parts of human life.

questions.question: What kind of being alone can intentionally create and direct things?
questions.answer: Only One with absolute power and perfect wisdom.

questions.question: What opposite role do created things have?
questions.answer: They are acted upon and display what has been made in them.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about purpose and benefit in creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that order is set for meaningful goals and useful results.

questions.question: Which abilities are necessary for making such purposeful order?
questions.answer: Knowledge, wisdom, will, and choice.

questions.question: What does the passage say this world-order proves about the Creator and Manager of beings?
questions.answer: It proves that He is one and acts by will and choice.

questions.question: According to the passage, what gives a thing existence, state, and form?
questions.answer: Power gives existence, will gives state, and choice gives form.

questions.question: Why are so many examples of “one” brought together in one paragraph?
questions.answer: To show that unity appears again and again in the world’s main supports.

questions.question: What conclusion comes from these examples of unity in the world?
questions.answer: The One who made and owns the world is also one.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Maker’s generosity?
questions.answer: It says He is very generous and treats living beings like honored guests.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the helpers serving those guests?
questions.answer: It describes them as many high-ranking and great servants.

questions.question: Name two Divine Names and two Divine actions mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: Compassionate and Nurturer are two Names; forming and nurturing are two actions.

questions.question: What does it mean that the Names and actions “embrace every place”?
questions.answer: It means their signs and effects are found throughout the whole world.

questions.question: How closely connected are the Names and actions according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are so closely connected that they seem to merge in one united working.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example where giving life appears along with creating, shaping, and providing?
questions.answer: One action in a thing is tied to many others, all working together from one source.

questions.question: What belief does the last sentence ask the reader to accept?
questions.answer: That the Doer behind all these Names and works is one, single, and unique.

questions.question: What does the passage say is built into all things?
questions.answer: A wise and exact order is built into all things.

questions.question: What are the two ends of the scale used to show this order?
questions.answer: The passage starts with the whole cosmos and ends with tiny details in the human body.

questions.question: What can we infer from order being found at every level of creation?
questions.answer: We can infer that one wise Planner is behind all levels of creation.

questions.question: Why does the passage deny that anything else can creatively interfere with things?
questions.answer: Because true creative control belongs only to the One with complete power and wisdom.

questions.question: What is the role of created things if they are not independent makers?
questions.answer: They receive effects and show signs of Allah’s action.

questions.question: Why are knowledge and wisdom linked to arranging things for benefits?
questions.answer: Because useful arrangement needs understanding of what is best.

questions.question: Why are will and choice also necessary?
questions.answer: Because selecting a certain way, shape, or result requires deciding and choosing.

questions.question: What does the varied order of the universe prove in a very clear way?
questions.answer: It proves that the Creator and Manager of all beings is one.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the coming into being of everything?
questions.answer: It says everything is brought into being by His power.

questions.question: How does a thing become this way rather than another way, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It becomes that way through His will and His choice.

questions.question: Why is the world described as a hospice instead of a random place?
questions.answer: To show that it is arranged with care, welcome, and provision for living beings.

questions.question: What do the one lamp, one time-marker, one drink, and one field all point toward?
questions.answer: They all point toward the oneness of the One who runs the world.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Master’s treatment of animate beings?
questions.answer: He cares for them as guests and serves them generously.

questions.question: What do the Divine Names, attributes, and actions have in common in this passage?
questions.answer: They are unified and their effects spread everywhere.

questions.question: What is one attribute named in the passage besides wisdom?
questions.answer: Mercy or grace.

questions.question: What happens when one Divine Name is seen at work in a thing?
questions.answer: Other Divine Names also appear there at the same time.

questions.question: Why is the example of Quickener important for understanding the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that life is given together with creating, shaping, and providing in one coordinated act.

questions.question: What final conclusion should a reader reach from the unity of these Names and deeds?
questions.answer: The One behind them must be one, single, and unique.

questions.question: What does the passage say about order in creation?
questions.answer: It says order is found everywhere in a wise and exact way.

questions.question: Which large pattern of the earth is mentioned as an example of this order?
questions.answer: Its daily and yearly turning.

questions.question: Which small bodily patterns are mentioned as examples?
questions.answer: A person’s facial features, the senses in the head, and the movement of blood cells.

questions.question: What kind of being is able to act on things intentionally and creatively?
questions.answer: Only the One with absolute power and absolute wisdom.

questions.question: What three descriptions are given for all other things?
questions.answer: They are receivers, places where His works appear, and passive.

questions.question: What is needed for arranging things toward goals and benefits?
questions.answer: Knowledge, wisdom, will, and choice are needed.

questions.question: What does the passage say the visible order of the cosmos proves?
questions.answer: It proves that the Creator and Director of all beings is one.

questions.question: What is done by power, by will, and by choice?
questions.answer: Power brings things into existence, will gives them a condition, and choice gives them a form.

questions.question: What is the world compared to in the third paragraph?
questions.answer: It is compared to a hospice.

questions.question: What does that comparison teach about the Maker?
questions.answer: It teaches that He is a caring and generous Master.

questions.question: Why does the passage keep saying many important things in the world are “one”?
questions.answer: To show signs of unity in how the world is managed.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from these many signs of unity?
questions.answer: The Maker and Master of the world is one.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the servants used to care for living beings?
questions.answer: They are many great and high-ranking servants.

questions.question: What are some of the Divine Names mentioned in the last part of the passage?
questions.answer: All-Wise, Compassionate, Giver of Forms, Disposer, Quickener, and Nurturer.

questions.question: What does the passage say about where these Names and actions are found?
questions.answer: Their signs are found in every part of the world.

questions.question: In what way do these Names and actions work together?
questions.answer: They complete one another and act in harmony.

questions.question: What combined set of Names appears when the giving of life is seen?
questions.answer: Giving life appears together with creating, shaping, and providing.

questions.question: What does the same pattern appearing everywhere prove about the Doer?
questions.answer: It proves the Doer is one, single, and unique.

questions.question: How do the speakers respond to this truth at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: They say they believe it and accept it.
